To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we present a novel representation of 3d shapes that can be used for classification using 2d CNNs, (b) we show that the 2D CNN can be used to learn features from the proposed representation, and (c) we show that our method is competitive with the state of the art in 3D shape classification.
We represent 3d shapes as multi-layered height-maps and use 2d convolutions for learning 3d shape descriptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three aspects: 1) a novel global representation for 3D shapes using MLH, 2) a novel view merging algorithm for combining view dependent descriptors from multiple views, and 3) a new application of 2d CNN for the classification of 3D shape categories.
